To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the best cache compression scheme is not necessarily the one that assumes that all data are integers, and (2) the best compression scheme is the one that selects the compression scheme that best exploits value locality.

(i) a cache compression scheme that exploits value locality for data types with predefined fields (e.g., floating-point numbers) offers better performance than prior art, and (ii) a cache compression system that selects the best compression scheme, based only on the value locality of the data types, offers superior performance compared to prior art.

HyComp, a hybrid cache compression method, selects the best-perform-ing compression method, based on data-type prediction, for data types including pointers, integers, and floating-point numbers, offering superior performance in comparison to state-of-the-art compression schemes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving cache performance by exploiting data type locality, and our proposed method HyComp is a step in this direction.
the design of cache compression schemes that can adapt to the data types of a program.
the design of a cache compression scheme that exploits value locality for data types that are not necessarily fixed-size.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HyComp is a hybrid cache compression method that selects the best performing compression scheme, based heuristics that predicts data types.
HyComp, with the proposed floating point compression method, offers the best performance of any cache compression scheme in the state-of-the-art.

HyComp offers superior performance in a variety of applications, including a 2.5x reduction in miss rate and 1.6x reduction in energy-delay product, in comparison with the best-performing prior-art cache compression scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HyComp is a novel cache compression scheme that exploits value locality for all data types, and is thus applicable to a wider range of applications than prior art.
HyComp offers 2-4 times the performance of prior art in terms of miss rate, while using 1.3 times the energy and 1.2 times the area of prior art.
HyComp offers 1.5x higher cache hit rate, 1.5-3x higher cache compression ratio and 1.2-1.5x lower cache miss penalty in comparison with prior-art cache compression methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cache compression can be made more effective if the data type of the data being compressed can be determined at runtime.
data-type-specific compression schemes can be combined to achieve superior cache compression performance.
the design-time assumption on value locality is a key factor in determining cache compression performance.
